hypothesis: Across oceanic islands, the share of native vascular plant species that are endemic to the island is high, and it is higher on oceanic islands than on comparable mainland regions or continental-shelf islands of similar area.
pass_criterion: Using GIFT checklists of native seed plants, the median endemic fraction (endemic species / native species) across oceanic islands (volcanic or atoll, never connected to a continent) is at least 0.20. It must also exceed the median for mainland regions of similar area (matched within a factor of 2 in km²) by at least 0.10, with a one-sided Mann-Whitney p < 0.01. At least 30 oceanic islands with at least 20 native species each must be included, and at least 10% of them must have an endemic fraction of 0.5 or more.
fail_criterion: The median endemic fraction on oceanic islands is below 0.10, or it does not exceed the area-matched mainland median by at least 0.05, or the Mann-Whitney test gives p >= 0.05. Any one of these refutes the claim.
interpretation: Darwin's 'oceanic islands' map to GIFT island regions with a geology/origin attribute of oceanic, as opposed to continental fragments. 'Number of kinds of inhabitants is scanty' maps to native species richness. 'Endemic species' maps to species whose GIFT native range is restricted to that single island region. 'Extremely large relative to area' is tested by comparing against area-matched mainland regions, because endemism rises with area in general. The modern reinterpretation is that GIFT covers only vascular plants, not whole faunas, and uses present-day taxonomy. The claim as Darwin stated it covers all inhabitants, so a plant-only test covers only part of its scope. I did not confirm the exact GIFT field names for endemism, island origin or area. The test would use the GIFT API/R package (checklist and species-by-region tables, with endemic-to-region status and region metadata) once those fields are confirmed.

dataset.name: GIFT – Global Inventory of Floras and Traits
dataset.publisher: University of Göttingen (Biodiversity, Macroecology and Biogeography)
dataset.why_it_fits: Search results describe GIFT as a database of regional plant checklists covering island and mainland regions, with native, endemic and naturalized floristic status. It is reachable through an R package, so endemic fraction per island region can be compared with area-matched mainland regions. I did not verify the endemism and island-origin fields on the landing page itself. I also fetched the Dryad record 'Species richness and phylogenetic structure of 249 global islands' (doi 10.5061/dryad.h44j0zpp5) and rejected it because it describes no endemic species counts.
